title: Allowing a `Path` object for `restart` for `Optimizer` (again) by fixing `Optimizer.todict` (closes #1851)
body:
closes #1851

## Summary

This MR fixes the above issue by converting `restart` into `str` in the `Optimizer.todict` method.

## Details

I found the issue in #1851 has been introduced in !3899 (abc2c1a12e26948bd1693deaba5c5c1871ef23a8), more specifically e70a5056ff97dec4e3e15519f4da69890fc911c0.

The origin of the issue is that, in the `Optimizer.todict` method, we set `restart` as a dictionary value as is, but a `Path` object cannot be converted to a JSON-compatible dictionary value.

In ASE 3.26.0, the issue did not happen (or not visible) because the `todict` method is called only in the beginning from `Dynamics.attach` ([here](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.26.0/ase/optimize/optimize.py?ref_type=tags#L185)) via `Dynamics.__init__` ([here](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.26.0/ase/optimize/optimize.py?ref_type=tags#L130-134)), where `restart` has not been defined yet (it is set in `Optimize.__init__` *after* `super().__init__`) and therefore not set in the `description` dictionary.
After !3899, on the other hand, the `todict` method is called at every step [here](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/merge_requests/3899/diffs#201b79af7d56c4d20c4b58814a15b0399dd67888_112_172), even after the `restart` has been defined, and if `restart` is not `str`, the issue in #1851 is raised.

In the present MR, I fix this by converting `restart` into `str` in the `Optimizer.todict` method, which should work also for the `Path` object.
We do not have to check the exsistence of `restart` with `hasattr`, because in `Optimizer` it should exist anyway.

@AndrewRosen, @askhl could you maybe have a look? Since a `Path` object for `restart` worked in 3.26.0, it would be nice to fix before releasing 3.27.0.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Thanks a lot @yuzie007.  Looks very good so I'll merge.

(Normally it's considered bad practice to save paths in the first place: It can be a security problem if the path reveals something about the host machine, and saving a path is also often questionable because files can very well be moved.  So in my opinion we should probably stop saving this piece of information altogether.)

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The author suggests stopping the saving of path information altogether, implying a code change should be made.

comments.author: AndrewRosen
comments.body:
@yuzie007 thanks! There is one small breaking change here.

```python
from ase.build import bulk
from ase.optimize import BFGS
from pathlib import Path
from ase.calculators.emt import EMT

atoms = bulk("Cu")
atoms.calc = EMT()
dyn = BFGS(atoms, trajectory="opt.traj", restart=None)
dyn.run()
assert dyn.todict()['restart'] is None
```

Whereas before, `dyn.todict()['restart']` would be `None`, now it is the `str` form of `"None"`.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment identifies a breaking change/bug where `restart=None` now serializes to the string 'None' instead of `None`, implying this should be fixed.
